function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Out of decision budget with the block still on the table. Four close attempts (steps 290, 447, 649, 819) all latched the jaws empty (measured gripper 0.015-0.018) even though the side/front views showed the block inside the jaw span; the only intermediate reading (0.18 at step 649) meant the pads pinched the block edge and it slipped out when I lifted. The last side view (step 819) confirms the red block resting on the table and the bowl untouched, so nothing of the task is complete.", "hindsight": "Concrete facts for a future attempt on this rig. (1) Control-step accounting: chunk length = max over dimensions of |target - last measured| / rate, with Cartesian rate ~30 mm/step but gripper ~0.012 units/step, while the arm physically tracks only ~5-10 mm/step. So a small commanded delta buys 1-5 steps and almost no motion. Trick that worked: put an intermediate gripper target (0.45 or 0.7) in the same move_to - it keeps the current latch (open/closed) but stretches the chunk to 44 steps; a full 0<->1 gripper change gives ~80 steps. Use that on every move or the arm never settles at the commanded pose. (2) Geometry: table top z=0.80; the robot base is at negative x (reach direction is +x); side camera horizontal = x with image-right = -x (base appears right), front camera horizontal = y, wrist camera image-right = -y (verified twice: +0.076 m and +0.035 m camera moves in y shifted the block +30 px and +17 px right). The wrist camera is tilted forward, so the point directly under the gripper projects at the bottom edge, not the image centre - never read xy offsets off the wrist centre; use the two fixed cameras. (3) Gripper: closes along world y at yaw=0; measured 1.0 = fully open (~8 cm), 0.015-0.02 = fully closed on nothing. eef_pos is well above the fingertip plane (about 4 cm), and the pads sit further back in -x than eef_pos, so aligning eef_pos over the block centre leaves the pads clipping the block corner. (4) The block migrates: every forward/down approach nudged it +x, ending about 10 cm from where it started, so re-triangulate from both fixed cameras before each close instead of reusing an old estimate. (5) Strategy: with only 20 calls, do not spend 5 on calibration; the descent alone ate 8 calls because of the slow tracker. Plan is 1 call to hover over the block, 1 padded call to descend to z~0.83 with jaws open, 1 to close, then transfer."}
